question: For a preactivation residual network in the depth-muP scaling, can the joint infinite-width and infinite-depth feature-learning dynamics be described rigorously despite the forward-backward dependence created by training, and does a neural-field-depth model that decouples forward and backward weights retain the correct limit?

key_findings.claim: The analysis is for a narrowly specified one-hidden-layer-per-block preactivation ResNet whose residual increment is scaled by 1/sqrt(Ln) and whose stream-SGD learning rate is eta_c n.
key_findings.evidence: Equation (1) defines h_l=h_{l-1}+(Ln)^(-1/2)W_l phi(h_{l-1}) and f=n^(-1)v^T h_L; Equation (2) applies one fresh example per update with learning rate eta=eta_c n. These scalings make both initialization fluctuations and feature-learning updates survive as width and depth grow.

key_findings.claim: The paper proves a genuine negative result for the postactivation alternative at fixed width: under a positive-dominance condition, an expected hidden-state coordinate diverges with depth despite 1/sqrt(L) residual scaling.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 3.1 lower-bounds E[h_(L,i)] by c1(1+c1/sqrt(Ln))^L ||x||/sqrt(d)+c2 sqrt(L). At fixed width this grows at least as sqrt(L) when c2>0 and as exp(Theta(sqrt(L/n))) when c1>0. The authors therefore restrict the remaining theory to preactivation blocks; Appendix B gives the proof and Appendix G.4 shows a finite-width ReLU contrast.

anchors.section: Appendix B Proof of the Postactivation Result
Appendix G.4 Preactivation versus Postactivation, Figure 4

key_findings.claim: At initialization, conditional Gaussian projection shows that the reused-weight forward-backward dependence becomes negligible coordinatewise, and the gradient-independence approximation has a uniform-in-depth O(1/n) squared-Wasserstein error for the backward state.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 4.1 represents the correlated backward multiplication as an aligned component plus a Gaussian component in the orthogonal complement of the exposed forward direction. Proposition 4.2 bounds W2 squared between each true backward coordinate g_(l,i) and its independent-backward-matrix counterpart by C/n uniformly over layers. Theorem 4.3 then has independent Brownian forward/backward drivers. Appendices C and D derive the representation and moment recursion.

key_findings.claim: The initialization limit is a coupled forward/backward stochastic differential equation with independent Brownian drivers, with total squared-Wasserstein error O(1/n+1/L) under the stated smoothness conditions.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.3 identifies the limiting processes and gives Equation (11), a coordinatewise W2-squared bound C(1/n+1/L). The proof combines the width approximation, stochastic-depth convergence, and triangle inequality; Appendix F supplies the depth discretization argument.

anchors.section: 4.3 Infinite Width-and-Depth Limit, Theorem 4.3 and Equation (11)
Appendix F Convergence of Stochastic Depth Dynamics

key_findings.claim: Training creates an explicit same-layer forward-backward correlation correction through products of a weight matrix with its transpose; a per-layer O(L^-2) term accumulates to O(L^-1) amplitude, while the squared accumulated coupling is O(L^-2).
key_findings.evidence: After one update, Propositions 5.1-5.2 and Equations (15)-(19) isolate the correction C_l produced when a later forward pass encounters W_l W_l^T terms inherited from backpropagation. The discussion says each layer contributes order L^-2 and the sum has order L^-1. Corollary 5.7 and Equation (28) bound the second moment of the accumulated sum by C/L^2. These are different quantities, so an unqualified 'O(L^-2) coupling' description is ambiguous.

anchors.section: 5.1 Forward-Backward Correlation after One Update, Propositions 5.1-5.2

key_findings.claim: The neural-field-depth construction is a controlled gradient-independence replacement: it decouples forward and backward Gaussian drivers and retains their learned within-family covariance kernels, while deliberately omitting the reused-weight C corrections after showing that their accumulated effect vanishes with depth.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 5.3 introduces independent forward and backward Brownian families with covariations Sigma and Theta and contains no C term. Proposition E.1 first writes the true fixed-depth width limit with explicit C corrections; Corollary 5.7 then bounds the difference created by omitting their layerwise sum. The tractability comes from separating covariance structure that survives from reused-weight corrections that are depth-suppressed.

key_findings.claim: The post-training theorem is conditional and sequential: for each fixed finite number of SGD steps K, width tends to infinity first and depth second, assuming the neural-field dynamics exist and their covariance matrices remain uniformly nondegenerate.
key_findings.evidence: Assumption 5.4 requires Lipschitz regularity, existence of the neural-field-depth recursion, and uniform lower eigenvalue bounds. Remark 5.5 explicitly leaves a complete existence theory open. Theorem 5.6 takes n to infinity for fixed L and then L to infinity; Corollary 5.7 gives an O(1/L) depth error after the width limit. The paper does not prove a joint n,L limit, the reverse order after training, a finite-width post-training rate, or a growing training horizon.

key_findings.claim: The broad novelty statement that prior tensor-program and dynamical-mean-field analyses do not explicitly characterize training-induced forward-backward correlation is too strong.
key_findings.evidence: The introduction and related-work discussion use lack of an explicit characterization to motivate the paper. Yet the current official Tensor Programs VI record, arXiv:2310.02244v5, explicitly decomposes W y into a Gaussian ket plus a correlation term, describes the post-update path W_l^T z followed by W_l W_l^T z', and carries named Gamma/C correlation corrections through its infinite-depth feature-learning recursions. The present paper may sharpen that mechanism into a conditional finite-width projection and an O(L^-2) second-moment estimate for its model, but it is not the first explicit identification of W W^T training correlation.

key_findings.claim: One proof uses materially stronger activation regularity than the corresponding main-text proposition states.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 4.2 on page 5 is stated with phi' Lipschitz. In Appendix D.2, Proposition D.5 assumes phi' and phi'' are bounded and the proof repeatedly controls the second-derivative diagonal matrix D. Theorem 4.3 adds that phi and phi' are Lipschitz, which controls a differentiable phi' only indirectly and still does not state the classical twice-differentiable assumptions used in that proposition. ReLU, used in the experiments, is outside this smooth proof regime.

anchors.section: Appendix D.2, Proposition D.5 and Second-Derivative Bounds

key_findings.claim: The finite-K width-limit extension is asserted more generally than it is derived in the appendix.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix E derives the one-update correction explicitly, then Proposition E.1 states the finite-K tensor-program representation and says the same mechanism extends via pairwise correction terms. Appendix F in turn announces a one-sample presentation for ease of exposition. A complete inductive derivation for arbitrary K and the stream of distinct samples is not written out, so this is a proof-presentation gap rather than a demonstrated counterexample to the theorem.

anchors.section: Appendix E-to-F Transition and One-Sample Simplification

key_findings.claim: Appendix C contains a local layer-index inconsistency in the one-update conditional-Gaussian derivation.
key_findings.evidence: The displayed shorthand around Equation (43) uses x_l^(1) where the main recursion in Equation (12) and Proposition 5.1 require the previous-layer state x_(l-1)^(1); it also sets the local variables using layer l rather than l-1. The surrounding derivation and later formulas indicate a typographical index error, but Equation (43) is not literally consistent as printed.

key_findings.claim: CIFAR-10 experiments are consistent with the predicted width/depth scaling and with standard-versus-decoupled loss alignment, but they do not establish the post-training joint-limit theorem that is absent from the analysis.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 1 plots mean-square discrepancies versus width and depth at initialization and after 30 epochs and visually tracks an O(1/n+1/L) reference. Figure 2 compares standard and decoupled loss trajectories at width 128; Appendix Figure 5 repeats the comparison at width 256. The curves are not accompanied by tabulated values, confidence intervals, a reverse-order limit experiment, or hidden-law diagnostics. Appendix G says the default experiments use minibatches of 128, whereas the theorem is formulated for stream SGD with one fresh example per step.

key_findings.claim: The covariance diagnostic is encouraging but does not verify the theorem's uniform nondegeneracy assumption.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 reports minimum covariance eigenvalues during online batch-one training for four-hidden-layer networks at widths 512-4096 over five seeds. A finite collection of shallow, finite-width trajectories cannot establish a lower bound uniform in depth, time, and all covariance blocks; the narrowest network also approaches small eigenvalues. The figure is therefore a stress check, not a proof of Assumption 5.4.

method.core_idea: Expose each reused Gaussian weight matrix conditionally on all earlier forward and backward computations, isolate the correction that training creates, and justify dropping that correction only after proving that depth-muP suppresses its accumulated effect; the resulting neural field keeps learned covariance structure but uses decoupled forward/backward drivers.
method.mechanism: At initialization, Gaussian conditioning decomposes the reused-matrix action into an independent innovation plus projections onto previously exposed directions; moment estimates make the relevant backward-coordinate discrepancy negligible uniformly across depth and yield independent Brownian forward/backward drivers. Under feature-learning SGD, the update inserts past backward vectors into W_l, so a future pass contains W_l W_l^T contractions. A tensor-program width limit first produces Gaussian recursions with explicit C terms. The NFD candidate omits C but retains the Sigma/Theta covariance kernels; stochastic-depth estimates bound the omitted accumulated correction and take L to infinity. Discrete Gronwall inequalities and Wasserstein couplings control the remaining errors.
assumptions: The architecture is a preactivation residual network with one random square matrix per block and residual scale 1/sqrt(Ln); the readout and learning-rate scalings are those in Equations (1)-(2).
Weights and readout coordinates are independently Gaussian at initialization, and the data and initial hidden coordinates satisfy the moment conditions used in Appendices C-F.
The number K of stream-SGD updates is fixed as width and depth grow; the proof does not cover K increasing with n or L.
The width limit is taken before the depth limit after training. Initialization has a quantitative joint error, but post-training reverse-order or arbitrary joint paths are not proved.
The loss derivative and activation regularity satisfy Assumption 5.4; derivative bounds used in Appendix D additionally require smoothness through a bounded second derivative.
Every covariance matrix inverted in the conditional projections remains uniformly positive definite over layers and the fixed training horizon.
The neural-field-depth recursion exists with the required moments; Remark 5.5 treats a complete existence/uniqueness theory as future work.
The theoretical optimizer is stream SGD with one fresh training example per step, not the minibatch-128 procedure used for several CIFAR-10 plots.

The postactivation divergence proposition requires its positive-dominance hypothesis and is a fixed-width depth statement, not a universal result for every postactivation architecture or joint scaling.

techniques.role: Decomposes a Gaussian weight matrix conditioned on its prior forward/backward uses into a fresh innovation and explicit low-rank correlation projections.
Couples the true initialization recursion to one using independent forward and backward matrices and bounds their coordinatewise squared-Wasserstein discrepancy uniformly in depth.
Tracks the W_l W_l^T terms induced by SGD and names the non-Gaussian correction C rather than discarding it under a gradient-independence heuristic.
Uses independent forward/backward Gaussian fields and retains their learned covariance kernels while omitting the separately bounded reused-weight C correction.
Converts the finite-width, finite-training-step computation graph into recursive Gaussian variables plus correlation corrections before depth is sent to infinity.
Treats residual layers as an Euler discretization and proves convergence to continuous-depth stochastic dynamics.
Combines width coupling and depth discretization errors to obtain initialization O(1/n+1/L) and post-width-limit O(1/L) squared-Wasserstein bounds.
Prevents local conditional-projection and discretization errors from growing uncontrollably across residual layers.
Empirically monitors the smallest covariance eigenvalue because the conditional Gaussian formulas require stable inverses.

limitations: Author-stated: The post-training result is a sequential width-then-depth limit and does not establish commutativity or a general joint scaling path.
Author-stated: The number of training steps K is fixed; long-time optimization, convergence of training, and K growing with model size are not covered.
Author-stated: A complete existence theory for the neural-field-depth dynamics is deferred, even though existence is part of Assumption 5.4.
Author-stated: Uniform covariance nondegeneracy is assumed and only probed empirically in small finite networks.
Reviewer-identified: The main theory covers a one-matrix preactivation ResNet, not multi-layer blocks, normalization, convolutional weight sharing, attention, Transformers, or modern optimizer state.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix D's bounded-second-derivative proof requirements are stronger than the nearby headline statement, excluding nonsmooth ReLU used in the experiments.
Reviewer-identified: The arbitrary-finite-K and distinct-stream-sample extensions are sketched after a one-update/one-sample derivation rather than proved in the same level of detail.

Reviewer-identified: CIFAR-10 figures provide visual scaling guides but no numerical tables, uncertainty intervals, reverse-order experiment, or direct measurement of the hidden-law Wasserstein quantities.
Reviewer-identified: Several empirical comparisons use minibatches of 128 although the theorem is formulated for one fresh example per update.
Reviewer-identified: The work characterizes an asymptotic approximation but does not show that its coupling changes optimization speed, generalization, robustness, or practical architecture design.
failure_modes: Postactivation residual blocks satisfying Proposition 3.1's positive-dominance condition can develop diverging expected coordinates; at fixed width the displayed c1 term scales as exp(Theta(sqrt(L/n))) rather than as exp(Theta(L)).
If a covariance block becomes singular or nearly singular, the conditional projections and inverse-covariance coefficients used by the neural field become unstable and Assumption 5.4 fails.
Nonsmooth activations such as ReLU violate the classical second-derivative bounds used in Appendix D, so the stated proof cannot be applied verbatim even if finite experiments look stable.
Training for K that grows with width/depth can accumulate correlation and approximation errors outside the fixed-horizon bounds.
Taking depth first, sending width and depth jointly along an unfavorable path, or using finite width after training may retain correlations not controlled by Theorem 5.6.
Minibatch reuse, momentum, Adam, weight decay, normalization, and tied weights can introduce dependence paths absent from the stream-SGD tensor program.
The O(L^-2) phrase can be misapplied to amplitude: the per-layer correction is O(L^-2), its accumulated amplitude is O(L^-1), and only the squared accumulated term is O(L^-2).
Finite loss-curve agreement may conceal discrepancies in hidden states, gradients, or rare covariance directions because the experiments do not measure the complete joint law.
reusable_insights: When the same random matrix appears in forward and backward computation, condition on its earlier uses and separate a fresh Gaussian innovation from finite-rank projection terms instead of assuming independence wholesale.
A useful decoupled surrogate can retain learned covariance kernels while omitting a reused-weight correction only when that omitted term is isolated and bounded separately.
Always distinguish a local layer correction, the amplitude of its layerwise sum, and the second moment of that sum; the powers of depth need not match.

For residual architectures, a width approximation and an Euler/stochastic-depth approximation can be coupled separately, then combined with a triangle inequality to expose which scale controls each error.
Uniform covariance eigenvalue bounds are a structural prerequisite, not a technical footnote; diagnostics should target the exact blocks and training horizon used in the proof.
A claimed joint empirical rate should be labeled separately from a sequential theorem, especially when finite-width rates disappear after training.
Negative results for postactivation orderings can motivate architecture choices, but their hypotheses and order of limits must travel with the conclusion.
open_questions: Can the post-training result be strengthened to a quantitative finite-n, finite-L bound that permits joint or reversed limits?
Can existence, uniqueness, and uniform covariance nondegeneracy of the neural-field-depth recursion be proved from checkable data/activation conditions rather than assumed?
Does the finite-K correction expansion remain controlled when K scales polynomially with width or depth or when training approaches stationarity?
Can the proofs be extended rigorously to ReLU or other nonsmooth activations using generalized derivatives or smoothing limits?
How do minibatches, data reuse, momentum, Adam, weight decay, normalization, and convolutional or attention weight sharing alter the correlation correction?
Is there a fully written induction for the arbitrary-K tensor-program representation with distinct stream samples and all cross-step correction paths?
Can experiments directly estimate the predicted C terms, hidden/gradient joint laws, and Wasserstein errors rather than only output MSE and loss curves?
Does suppressing or retaining the identified correlation measurably affect optimization, generalization, or hyperparameter transfer at practical widths and depths?
Which part remains distinct from the explicit Gamma/C correlation recursions in Tensor Programs VI after matching architecture, scaling, and notation?
Does postactivation divergence persist under normalization, learned residual gates, alternative depth scalings, or simultaneous n,L growth?

competitive_landscape.title: Tensor Programs VI: Feature Learning in Infinite-Depth Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Tensor Programs VI already derives infinite-width/infinite-depth feature-learning recursions and explicitly represents the correlation created when training produces W_l^T z and a later pass encounters W_l W_l^T z'. It names Gaussian-ket and Gamma/C correction terms. The present paper's defensible increment is a conditional finite-width Gaussian projection, a uniform initialization W2 rate, and a claimed O(L^-2) second-moment control/NFD approximation for its narrower ResNet—not first identification of the correlation.

competitive_landscape.title: Depthwise Hyperparameter Transfer in Residual Networks: Dynamics and Scaling Limit
competitive_landscape.difference: This dynamical-mean-field analysis studies depth-muP residual-network training, simultaneous width/depth scaling, feature-learning dynamics, and hyperparameter transfer. The present work gives more explicit conditional control of a forward-backward correction but covers a simpler block and only a sequential fixed-K post-training limit.

competitive_landscape.title: Width and Depth Limits Commute in Residual Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Hayou and Yang prove width/depth commutativity for residual networks at initialization and characterize covariance behavior. The present paper adds backward variables and feature-learning correlation, but its post-training theorem no longer proves commutativity and instead takes width before depth.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICML 2023, PMLR 202 version of record, pp. 12700-12723

competitive_landscape.title: The Neural Covariance SDE: Shaped Infinite Depth-and-Width Networks at Initialization
competitive_landscape.difference: The Neural Covariance SDE develops joint depth-width initialization limits for shaped networks through a covariance SDE. The present work specializes to depth-muP preactivation ResNets, includes backward dynamics, and attempts a fixed-horizon feature-learning extension via explicit training corrections.

competitive_landscape.title: Infinitely Deep Neural Networks as Diffusion Processes
competitive_landscape.difference: This work established diffusion-process limits for randomly initialized deep residual networks. The present paper adds a width-dependent depth-muP scaling, backward dynamics, Wasserstein rates, and a training-dependent neural field rather than only a forward initialization diffusion.

competitive_landscape.title: Tensor Programs IV: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Tensor Programs IV supplies a master-theorem framework for feature learning under maximal-update parameterization at infinite width. The present paper relies on this line but adds an infinite-depth limit and explicit depth scaling; its theorem is correspondingly restricted to fixed training horizon and covariance regularity.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Limits of Wide Neural Networks with Weight Sharing: Gaussian Process Behavior, Gradient Independence, and Neural Tangent Kernel Derivation
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper formalizes when gradient independence is valid or invalid in wide networks with reused weights and derives correction behavior at initialization. The present work seeks a uniform-in-depth quantitative coupling and then tracks the new dependence created by feature-learning updates.

competitive_landscape.title: Tensor Programs II: Neural Tangent Kernel for Any Architecture
competitive_landscape.difference: Tensor Programs II provides a simple-check framework for gradient-independence calculations and NTK limits across architectures. The present work is in the feature-learning rather than frozen-kernel regime and focuses on the depth accumulation of an explicit forward-backward correction.

competitive_landscape.title: Mean Field Residual Networks: On the Edge of Chaos
competitive_landscape.difference: This work analyzes forward and backward signal propagation and stability in deep random residual networks through mean-field recursions. The present paper uses depth-muP and conditional Gaussian methods to obtain diffusion and feature-learning limits rather than an initialization stability analysis alone.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper presents the first rigorous joint infinite-width/infinite-depth characterization of feature-learning dynamics that explicitly resolves the training-induced forward-backward correlation, proves that its cumulative effect decays as O(L^-2), and justifies a neural-field-depth approximation.
novelty_assessment.evidence: For the specified preactivation depth-muP ResNet, the paper provides conditional Gaussian representations, an initialization O(1/n+1/L) squared-Wasserstein bound, explicit W_l W_l^T correction formulas after training, a width-then-depth fixed-K theorem under Assumption 5.4, and CIFAR-10 plots consistent with the approximation.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest supportable novelty is narrower: a conditional finite-width Gaussian decomposition with a uniform initialization rate, plus an explicit second-moment depth estimate and neural-field decoupling for a simple preactivation ResNet. Tensor Programs VI v5 already explicitly identifies the same post-update W_l W_l^T forward-backward mechanism and carries Gamma/C corrections in infinite-depth feature-learning recursions, while prior DMFT work already studies depth-muP training limits. Moreover, the O(L^-2) phrase applies to each layer and to the second moment of the accumulated correction, not its accumulated amplitude; the post-training result is conditional, sequential, fixed-K, and lacks a finite-width rate. The result remains technically interesting, but the priority and scope claims should be narrowed accordingly.
